text:
ria: FYI we saw another memory surge during the midnight rollout. root cause looks similar: shard residency not reclaiming after stream closes; fragmentation ticked up on 64GB hosts. posting quick action list.

sam: can you paste the short checklist so I can schedule infra change window?

owen: captured a short heap diff and a small flamegraph: jemalloc.retained is ~12% above rss, kv_residency_count grew 18% in 2 hours. linking artifacts shortly.

ria: actions: A1: run cross-region heap scan + jemalloc stats on canaries (owner @owen, due 2026-03-03) | A2: enforce idle-evict for shards >25m in staging (owner @sam, due 2026-03-02) | A3: prototype small background compactor with rate cap (owner @ria, due 2026-03-10) | A4: add alert kv_residency_heat for upward trend (owner @runbooks, due 2026-03-01)

sam: scheduling A2 for 2026-03-02 04:00 UTC to staging; will monitor kv_residency_size and p95.

owen: A1 started, dumps uploading to gs://redwood-perf/residency/2811112222/. will attach results here when ready.

perf-bot: test-run: staging load test 50 streams x 2h completed; no immediate OOMs; kv_fragmentation metric rose by 3%.

ria: note on rollout: prefer config-only canary first. compaction is higher-risk; add feature flag and allow quick toggle. rollback criteria: any p95 increase >15ms or error-rate spike.

runbooks: updated runbook "shard-residency-surge" with steps to run A1, how to flip idle-evict, and Slack escalation template. heuristic added: if jemalloc.retained / rss > 1.1 then prioritize compaction.

sam: will post staging validation results here after the deploy window.

ria: thanks team. reconvene Fri if A1 artifacts show fragmentation-heavy retention. update thread with blockers. :white_check_mark:
